long_biography.plain_text:
In 1988, Wolle left East Germany for the West after completing a doctorate in engineering. Although equipped with technical training, he lacked an established professional network there. Assignments for bearing maker SKF took him through difficult international markets. He then joined Siber Hegner in Hong Kong, beginning the Asian experience that would shape his working life.

Wolle ran Siber Hegner Group and oversaw its difficult corporate turnaround. The subsequent corporate combination with two neighbouring trading houses created DKSH, whose sales and profits multiplied under his leadership. The company's 2012 flotation converted years of operating work and personal equity risk into substantial wealth. Since leaving DKSH, Wolle has focused on board governance at logistics group Kuehne+Nagel and gear engineering specialist Klingelnberg, while allocating capital across selected growth businesses.
